newsitem.title: JAPAN: Indonesia central banker says worried over yen.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia central banker says worried over yen.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono told Reuters Financial Television in an interview on Monday that he is worried about the recent rise of the yen against the dollar, as much of the country's external debt is denominated in yen.
"We are concerned (about the rise of the yen) partly because our exposure for government debt to the Japanese yen is high, maybe close to 40 percent," said Djiwandono, governor of Bank Indonesia.
He also said the rupiah has depreciated three to five percent since the early 1980s, and said he has been "comfortable" with the depreciation.
"When we talk about the depreciation of the rupiah, it's part of our efforts to support the export drive to help our competitiveness in exports," he said.
Djiwandono said there is room for lower interest rates in Indonesia when inflation is under control. "Once inflation is under control, room for lower interest rates is there," he said.
However, interest-rate trends in major nations such as the United States are complicating Indonesia's moves on interest rates.
"There is a worldwide trend for higher interest rates now. These kinds of things are sometimes complicating our aim of trying to reduce interest rates back home in Indonesia," he said.
He added that Indonesia is "more or less" on track in achieving its inflation target. "Our aim is even (an inflation rate of) five percent, and we approach it in stages," he said.
